$comment: Source is TypeScript now (src/host/*.ts, src/client/*.ts, plus src/shared/wire.ts — the wire contract both halves read, TYPE-ONLY), and every .ts file is type-checked unconditionally — `checkJs` only governs plain .js files, of which src/ has none (a .js under src/ would need a top-level '// @ts-check' pragma to be checked at all). strict/noImplicitAny stay false, so untyped parameters are implicit-any and pass: the ONE shape that does not is a parameter WITH a default initializer, which is typed from that initializer — give it an explicit annotation instead of JSDoc (in a .ts file `@param`/`@type` are comments, not type sources; see src/host/lifecycle.ts, src/host/index.ts). strictNullChecks IS on project-wide since 2026-10-02 (docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md §8, the graduation-track endpoint): the per-file allowlist (tsconfig.strict-null.json) reached 100% of src, so the split is retired and the flag is stated here, in the one config that gates the push. noEmit:true means this check never produces artifacts — the build is tsdown's job (test/build-gate.mjs). Run it with `npm run typecheck`; since the 8 strict flags landed it is also part of `npm test` via test/typecheck-gate.mjs, which runs the tsc pinned in devDependencies (loud SKIP when typescript is absent, same rule as build-gate). erasableSyntaxOnly is TRUE and is the one flag here that exists for the TEST harness rather than for the types: the 26-segment `test` chain runs on bare `node` with no bundler, no loader and no dependencies (no tsx/jiti/vitest anywhere in package.json), importing `src/host/*.ts` directly (52 such imports), so Node's strip-only loader is the real compiler for every module a test can reach. Strip-only mode cannot execute `enum`, `namespace`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`) or angle-bracket assertions (`<T>expr`) — it fails at RUNTIME with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX — while plain tsc accepts all four, so without this flag a `.ts` file can typecheck clean and only explode when a suite imports it. The flag moves that to a compile-time error (TS1294). It costs nothing today: the sources are already fully erasable (verified by flipping the flag on and running both `npm run typecheck` and the full `npm test`, both green). Because test/typecheck-gate.mjs runs tsc on every push, this flag is enforced from the moment it lands — no gate change needed. tsconfig.strict-null.json `extends` this file, so it inherits the flag. Note it is NOT about .tsx: this project has none, and Node cannot execute .tsx under any flag anyway; the rule it encodes is simply that anything a bare-Node test imports must be erasable.
